metric_descriptions.input_truncated: 1 when a local model saw only part of the article, because it was longer than the model's encoder window (1,024 tokens for BART) and was cut, else 0. Those items are a different task from the hosted arms' full-article ones.
metric_descriptions.n_pairs: Pairwise mode: how many of the article's sampled pairs the experts ranked apart, the pairs pair_agreement is averaged over.
metric_descriptions.pair_agreement: Pairwise mode: among the sampled pairs of an article's summaries that the experts rank apart, the share where the judge preferred the summary the experts prefer; a tie counts half and an unreadable answer 0. Chance is 0.5.
metric_descriptions.parsed: Whether the reply could be read as an answer in the task's format: 1 or 0 per item, so its mean is the share readable (for the SummEval judges, the share of the four dimensions that came back readable). An unreadable reply scores 0 on the quality metrics, never skipped.
metric_descriptions.rho: Spearman's rho between the judge's scores and the experts' ratings of an article's 16 summaries, averaged over the four dimensions: kept for comparison with the literature.
metric_descriptions.rho_coherence: Spearman's rho with the experts' coherence ratings across an article's 16 summaries (0 when the judge returned no coherence scores).
metric_descriptions.rho_consistency: Spearman's rho with the experts' consistency ratings across an article's 16 summaries (0 when the judge returned no consistency scores).
metric_descriptions.rho_fluency: Spearman's rho with the experts' fluency ratings across an article's 16 summaries (0 when the judge returned no fluency scores).
metric_descriptions.rho_relevance: Spearman's rho with the experts' relevance ratings across an article's 16 summaries (0 when the judge returned no relevance scores).

tau.details: Per article the judge scores 16 summaries on coherence, consistency, fluency and relevance. For each dimension its scores are correlated with the expert ratings by tau-b, which corrects for ties on both sides (an LLM judge's integer scores tie often); a dimension the judge did not return, or a constant side, counts 0. tau is the mean of the four, then over articles: agreement with people on ordering summaries, not a summary's quality.
tau.summary: Kendall's tau-b between the judge's scores and the experts' ratings of an article's 16 summaries, averaged over the four dimensions.

metric_descriptions.tau_coherence: Kendall's tau-b with the experts' coherence ratings across an article's 16 summaries (0 when the judge returned no coherence scores).
metric_descriptions.tau_consistency: Kendall's tau-b with the experts' consistency ratings across an article's 16 summaries (0 when the judge returned no consistency scores).
metric_descriptions.tau_fluency: Kendall's tau-b with the experts' fluency ratings across an article's 16 summaries (0 when the judge returned no fluency scores).
metric_descriptions.tau_relevance: Kendall's tau-b with the experts' relevance ratings across an article's 16 summaries (0 when the judge returned no relevance scores).
metric_descriptions.tie_rate: Share of the 120 summary pairs the judge scored equal, averaged over the dimensions it returned: how often it could not tell two summaries apart.
metric_descriptions.top1: Pick mode: how often the judge's pick of the best of an article's 16 summaries is a summary the experts rate best (highest mean over the four dimensions; ties among the experts form the best set). 1 for a correct single pick; a pick of several scores the share of them that are correct; an unreadable pick scores 0.
metric_descriptions.top1_chance: Pick mode: what a random pick scores on the article, the share of its 16 summaries the experts rate best (|best set| / 16). A judge's top1 is read against its mean.
metric_descriptions.truncated: 1 when the provider cut the reply off at the token ceiling (finish_reason "length", and in most adapters a completion that reached 98% of max_tokens), else 0. An arm with truncated above 0 has scores that partly describe the ceiling, not the model.
